title: ALMOST HUMAN
summary: A man does up his collar and tie, first in profile and then facing us. Other people's small gestures begin and do not finish: a woman's hand rises to her mouth, a driver looks at his watch and away, a boy finds a loose button. The film returns to the first man, hands at the knot, and holds.

reviews.text:
VERDICT: inconclusive, leaning reference stronger. I can't hear the film, so I couldn't judge the room-sound rhythm.

Before the brief: at 0-10s a man in suspenders adjusts his tie (0-5s, profile; 6-10s, frontal). The collar gesture reads as complete and the repetition is held. Then at 11-15s a woman cries into her fist, with the voice asking "Isn't there a better way to manage ourselves?" at 12.4s. That line pins an emotional meaning on a gesture, which is the opposite of the film's stated intent. The film looks like a montage of period-instruction footage, narrated by one lecturing voice.

Largest gap: no memory-activating return. The sheet shows no return to the striped-wall setting after 10s. It ends on a standing man (44-47s) that has not appeared before, and the 43.1s line "It's worth a try" closes the film on a moral. The brief's 75s was not met either; the sheet runs 48s.

Repairs:
1. Add the return to the striped wall (0-10s) after the last gesture, at about 40-48s, with the man absent or his tie finished. Check that the same frame reappears after the 38s shot.
2. Cut or move the 12.4-15.1s line over the woman. Check that 11-15s has no speech.
3. The wristwatch (18-19s) is a 2s hold on an object with no visible outcome. Extend it with the next gesture's start, or cut to 20s with the driver's head turn. Check that something changes across the cut.

Strength to protect: the 0-10s collar adjustment. It is long and complete, and the profile-to-frontal shift stays specific without music.
reviews.builder_note: True on the line pinned to a gesture and on the missing return; both repaired. The film is still shorter than the 75 s the proof asks for.

packet.note: the first cut, before any repair

repairs: Removed the spoken line from under the woman's gesture.
Replaced the closing shot with a return to the first man at the same wall, last frame held 3.6 s.

worked: Ten searches written as actions ('a man checks his wristwatch and looks away'), not emotions. Instruction and etiquette films answered best.
The long uncut collar sequence is a source film's own 'appearance' lesson, used almost whole because its pause after the adjustment is the point.
The 1927 silent clips carry raised hiss on purpose, so the cut never goes quiet.
failed: I could not see this film's contact sheets or filmstrips while cutting it: every image read returned a request-limit error. I cut from search titles, Whisper word timings, durations and loudness numbers. After the cut I checked each reason against frames of the final film and corrected five that described things the frames do not show (a hand 'climbing' to a collar, a slip 'pocketed', hands 'in the air').

A line from the source film ('Isn't there a better way to manage ourselves?') had been left over a woman's gesture and assigned her a feeling. The critic was right; I rebuilt the audio under that shot from the source's own sound around the line.
The first cut ended on a man not seen before and on a moral line. It now returns to the first man.
open: The proof wants one gesture whose outcome differs between two people inside a pair of shots; the cut shows differences in sequence, not as a pair.
